decisions.reason: The Hero V remains the approved architectural reference; asking the E and L forms to match its design language does not change the Hero V geometry.

The message reports that the implemented second V lost its already-required subtle right-arm reach, but it does not change that Requirement's client-confirmed value; the same-message runtime failure already captures the mismatch.
Peak alignment is an independent requirement directly introduced by an existing same-message Event and is not a consequence of the E and L letterform modification.
Removing Roman-style flares from the E and L forms does not alter the established signature terminal treatment shared by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.
The E and L customization decision does not change the requirement that the É accent be literally derived from the Hero V terminal.
The client changes the construction and terminal style of the E and L glyphs but does not establish a new kerning or spacing rule.
The E and L geometry refinement does not modify or resume the deferred champagne material treatment.
The message identifies loss of the second V's right-arm reach, not a change to its smaller, subordinate visual hierarchy.
The letterform feedback does not change the task-local obligation to include design rationale with review rounds.
The E and L design decision has no effect on the acceptable attachment formats for viewable proofs.
